D001-D008_h001.question_both:
For the last year or so, my wife keeps saying I’m “always on.” I feel like I’m constantly in motion, even when I’m just in my classroom—pacing, fiddling with markers, getting up and down during prep. I struggle to just sit and grade; I’ll start on one stack of papers, then remember an email, then suddenly I’m rearranging my desk instead. By the end of the day, I’ve half-finished ten different things.

In meetings, I catch myself talking way more than everyone else, jumping in before people finish, going off on tangents. Sometimes my students joke that I “never shut up,” and they’re not entirely wrong. My mind races ahead, and I feel like I have to get it all out before I lose the thought.

I’m also really easily thrown off. A noise in the hallway, a kid tapping a pen, or even my own random thoughts can pull me away from what I’m doing. Some weeks I feel more amped up than usual—like I’ve got extra energy and less need for sleep—other times I’m just tired but still restless and scattered. It’s getting harder to manage my workload and keep things straight.
D001-D008_h001.question_a:
Ever since I was a kid—teachers used to say it in elementary school—I’ve had trouble sitting still and staying focused. I remember getting in trouble for constantly fidgeting, wandering around the classroom, and blurting out answers. It never really went away. Even now, in my 40s, I feel like I’m always “on,” like there’s a motor running inside me. I pace around my classroom between periods and even at home my wife comments that I can’t just sit on the couch and relax.

At work, I struggle to keep things organized—lesson plans, grading, emails. I’ll start grading a stack of papers, get distracted by an email or a random thought, and then forget what I was doing. My mind drifts in the middle of students talking; it’s like my thoughts jump tracks constantly.

I also talk a lot—my colleagues joke that I can turn any quick chat into a long conversation. A few times a year I do get into these “high” moods where I feel extra energetic and sleep less, but even when I’m not in those phases, the distractibility, disorganization, restlessness, and excessive talking are there all the time.
D001-D008_h001.question_b:
For most of my adult life I’ve been pretty steady—organized enough to handle lesson plans, grading, coaching debate, that kind of thing. But about six months ago I started having these “up” periods that my wife says are totally unlike me. When those hit, that’s when everything goes off the rails.

During these spells I sleep maybe three or four hours and still feel wired, like I’m running on some invisible motor. At school I can’t sit still in the classroom; I’m pacing, popping into other rooms, starting a dozen projects at once. My desk turns into a disaster—half-finished unit plans, random Post-its everywhere—and I just can’t seem to put things in order even though I’m working nonstop.

My mind races. I jump from grading to redesigning the whole curriculum to thinking about starting a podcast. In the middle of teaching, I’ll lose the thread because some random idea pops into my head and pulls me away. I catch myself talking nonstop in class and at home, interrupting students and my wife, going on long tangents.  

When these “high” phases pass, I go back to my usual, more organized self. The distractibility and constant energy don’t stick around between those episodes.

I start one case note, get pulled off by an email or a random thought, and suddenly I’m down a rabbit hole and the note’s still unfinished an hour later. I double-book appointments or forget to call families back because I can’t keep everything straight, even with calendars and apps.

I’m constantly moving—bouncing my leg in meetings, pacing during phone calls. Coworkers joke that I never sit still. I talk a lot in team meetings, sometimes interrupting without meaning to, and then feel embarrassed later.

Lately I feel like I’m running on high gear most of the time. Even after long shifts, I’m pacing around truck stops instead of resting, like I can’t shut my body off. I talk a lot more than I used to—other drivers, clerks, anyone nearby—I’ll just keep going, hopping from one topic to another before they can really answer.

There are stretches where this “amped up” feeling gets stronger for days at a time, then it eases back a bit, but the trouble focusing and staying organized seems to hang around either way.
D001-D008_h003.question_a:
I’ve always been kind of restless, even as a kid. Teachers used to tell my parents I couldn’t sit still in class, always fidgeting, talking over people, getting up to sharpen a pencil ten times. It never really went away. Even now, at 46, I feel like I’ve got a motor running all the time. On my breaks I end up pacing around the truck stop instead of just sitting. Long hauls are hard because my mind jumps all over the place; I catch myself drifting off into random thoughts and then realize I’ve missed an exit or screwed up a route.

Paperwork and planning the loads are a mess for me. I put things off, lose track of what I’m supposed to do next, forget who I was supposed to call. My dispatchers complain my logs are disorganized or incomplete. I also talk a lot—once I start, it’s like I can’t shut up, even when I see people getting annoyed.

Every now and then I’ll have a couple days where I feel more upbeat and sleep less, but this scattered, restless feeling is there all the time, not just when my mood is up. It’s been like this my whole life.
D001-D008_h003.question_b:

But when I “flip on,” like now, everything changes. I barely sleep and feel wired, like my whole body’s revved up. On the road I can’t stick to one plan. I’ll start mapping out deliveries, then suddenly decide to rearrange the whole run, then forget what I was doing. My head keeps jumping to random ideas — business plans, fixing up the truck, calling my ex — and any little thing pulls my attention away.

I can’t sit still at truck stops; I’m pacing, moving, like I’ve got a motor in me. Dispatch keeps telling me to slow down because I’m talking their ear off on the phone, way more than usual, jumping from topic to topic. When these “high” periods pass, the restlessness and scatter just drop off and I go back to my usual self.

I’ve been having a really hard time keeping my head straight, especially this past year or so. In the workshop, I’ll measure something twice and still cut it wrong, or I’ll stain the wrong side of a panel because I just don’t catch the small details. Clients will email clear specs, and I’ll start a piece, then somehow jump to another project before finishing the first. I’ve got half-done tables and cabinets all over the place.

It feels like I can’t sit still, even when I’m exhausted. I’m pacing around the shop, starting three things at once, talking too fast if someone stops by. My sister says I’m “always on,” like I’m plugged into a socket. When I’m with people, I catch myself cutting them off or finishing their sentences, or I’ll butt into conversations that aren’t really mine without thinking about it, then feel awkward later.

Some weeks this revved-up feeling and scattered focus are much worse; other times I’m a bit more level, but I still drift off and leave tasks hanging. I can’t tell if it’s just stress, my personality, or something else.

Teachers always said I was “bright but scattered.” I’d rush through math sheets and miss stupid little things, like adding an extra zero, even when I knew how to do it. That’s kind of how my work is now with the furniture—if I don’t triple-check, I’ll misread a measurement or drill in the wrong place because my mind has already jumped to the next step.

Clients will text me their specs, and I’ll start a project full of energy, then halfway through I’ll realize I skipped a step or left something unfinished in the shop. It’s not that I don’t care; I lose the thread. Instructions, emails, even simple house stuff—laundry, bills—if it’s not right in front of me, it just falls off my radar.

I’m always moving—pacing in the shop, bouncing my leg, starting three tasks at once. Coworkers and my ex used to say I act like I’m “plugged in.” I cut people off a lot without meaning to, jump into conversations, answer before folks finish talking. 

I do have times when my mood goes up or down, but this restless, distracted feeling is there all the time, not just when I’m in a good or bad mood.

All of a sudden I barely sleep and I’m moving nonstop in the shop, like I’ve got a motor in me. I’m bouncing from one project to the next, talking over my assistant and even cutting off customers mid-sentence because I feel like I need to say everything at once. I can’t seem to slow down enough to listen properly.

At the same time, I’ve started making these stupid mistakes I never used to make—misreading measurements, forgetting to glue pieces, sending out half-finished quotes. I’ll start on a custom table and then abandon it halfway through because I’ve already jumped to a new idea. My ex-husband used to say I was meticulous; now I feel scattered only when I’m in this “amped up” state.

When this high energy dies down—which it has a couple times in the past—my focus and attention go back to normal. It’s only during these intense, revved-up periods that I get this distracted and restless.
